admission_rule: External evidence is never imported as FAE measurement. Each item records population/environment, period, relevance, limitations and directness.

items.source: Christian Decker, Roger Wattenhofer — Information Propagation in the Bitcoin Network
items.period: 2013 publication; measurements reflect early Bitcoin network/protocol
items.finding_relevant_to_fae: Empirically links propagation delay with blockchain forks and motivates measuring propagation tails rather than treating relay latency as incidental.
limitations: Bitcoin-specific topology and relay implementation
historical network conditions
10-minute Bitcoin interval differs from FAE 180s
does not measure FAE

items.source: Gervais et al. — On the Security and Performance of Proof of Work Blockchains
items.population_environment: PoW blockchain models parameterized with network propagation, block size, interval, adversarial strategies and eclipse effects
items.finding_relevant_to_fae: Supports joint treatment of consensus/network parameters: block interval, propagation, stale rate, throughput and adversarial strategy interact.
limitations: model assumptions differ from FAE implementation
not calibrated to FAE nodes or miners

items.source: Croman et al. — On Scaling Decentralized Blockchains
items.finding_relevant_to_fae: Warns that block-size/interval reparameterization is only part of throughput/latency scaling and must retain decentralization/network constraints.
limitations: Bitcoin-era measurements
different relay stack, payload and node population

items.finding_relevant_to_fae: Documents how reducing relay bandwidth can reduce propagation latency and consumer-grade bandwidth spikes; reinforces that block-time safety depends on relay design, not interval alone.
limitations: FAE does not inherit BIP152 by analogy
Bitcoin mempool/relay protocol differs

items.source: Meni Rosenfeld — Analysis of Bitcoin Pooled Mining Reward Systems
items.population_environment: Bitcoin solo and pooled mining reward systems
items.finding_relevant_to_fae: Formalizes mining reward variance and why pooling can reduce payout variance, directly motivating FAE's small-miner variance/pool-pressure frontier.
items.relevance: payout variance; pooling incentive; small miners
limitations: Bitcoin reward/pool mechanisms differ
does not include FAE participation or hardware objectives

items.source: Sapirshtein, Sompolinsky, Zohar — Optimal Selfish Mining Strategies in Bitcoin
items.population_environment: Bitcoin selfish-mining models including communication delay
items.finding_relevant_to_fae: Shows communication delay can change miner incentives and adversarial profitability; supports treating low-latency advantage as a decentralization/security variable.
items.relevance: latency advantage; miner concentration; fork competition
limitations: adversarial model differs from FAE
does not establish a FAE selfish-mining threshold

items.source: Thomas M. Harding — Real-Time Block Rate Targeting
items.finding_relevant_to_fae: Treats DAA responsiveness, stability and timestamp rules as coupled design variables, supporting F180-03/F180-04 separation from simple average block-time checks.
limitations: proposed algorithms are not the active FAE v4 DAA

items.source: Ilie et al. — Unstable Throughput: When the Difficulty Algorithm Breaks
items.population_environment: Bitcoin Cash DAA and coin-hopping simulations
items.finding_relevant_to_fae: Documents how DAA feedback can produce cyclic block times and unstable transaction throughput under miner switching.
limitations: BCH DAA and mining market differ from FAE
no direct mapping of observed amplitudes

items.source: Noda, Okumura, Hashimoto — An Economic Analysis of Difficulty Adjustment Algorithms in Proof-of-Work Blockchain Systems
items.population_environment: PoW DAA models, Bitcoin/BCH/ASERT analysis with endogenous hash-supply response
items.finding_relevant_to_fae: Shows DAA stability can depend on miner hash-supply response and compares slower epoch adjustment with newer approaches; supports explicit miner arrival/departure scenarios.
items.relevance: DAA stability; economic miner response; oscillation
limitations: FAE live 20-block ±2-bit algorithm is distinct
economic elasticity estimates are not transferable to FAE

items.source: Blockchain Stretching & Squeezing: Manipulating Time for Your Best Interest
items.population_environment: Bitcoin/Ethereum time and DAA manipulation models
items.finding_relevant_to_fae: Establishes that miner-controlled timing can interact with DAA/block rate strategically; supports an explicit adversarial timestamp frontier rather than assuming timestamps are passive metadata.
items.relevance: timestamp manipulation; DAA; adversarial miner incentives
limitations: attacks/uses depend on Bitcoin/Ethereum semantics and applications
not a direct exploit claim against FAE

synthesis: External literature supports the research architecture but supplies no direct FAE PASS.
Propagation delay is a security/decentralization variable, not merely a UX variable.
DAA stability must be tested under endogenous or switching hashrate, not only fixed hashrate.
Payout variance provides a rational pressure toward pooling, so reward frequency matters to FAE's household-hardware objective.
Timestamp rules and DAA must be evaluated jointly.
Network relay design can materially alter propagation; block interval alone does not determine stale pressure.
